title: Counterexamples to the Cooper–Spencer temporal-unimodality conjecture
shortTitle: A random-walk probability falls, then rises
oneLine: An exact dimension-26 counterexample and a written proof of failure in every dimension at least 64.
abstract: For simple symmetric lattice random walk, this unrefereed candidate gives an exact parity-restricted occupation-probability valley at times 65, 67 and 69 in dimension 26. A parity-sensitive Poissonisation lemma and rational Bessel bounds give counterexamples at (ceil(3d/5),0,...,0) for every integer d>=64. The threshold is sufficient, not optimal. Classical counting and transform machinery are explicitly distinguished from the counterexamples.

narration: Imagine a walker on a grid, choosing each step at random. Pick one destination and watch the chance of finding the walker there as time passes. Must that chance rise once and then fall? Cooper and Spencer conjectured that it does, after restricting attention to the times when the destination can actually be reached. This candidate gives an exact counterexample. In twenty-six dimensions, at one specified destination, the occupation probability falls between steps sixty-five and sixty-seven, then rises at step sixty-nine. The change is small, but it is certified by integer arithmetic, not a simulation or a floating-point guess. The paper also gives a written proof of counterexamples in every dimension at least sixty-four. It first studies a continuous-time walk and then uses a parity-sensitive argument to transfer the failure back to discrete time. The release includes the paper, exact counts, rational bounds, source code and tests. Classical counting and transform identities are credited as established tools. The work does not determine the smallest possible dimension or classify all destinations and modes. A bounded literature search does not certify historical priority. This is an unrefereed Evidence Press candidate dated September nineteenth, twenty twenty-six. The full paper and evidence are linked on the release page.
